description: Architect-adjacent. Reality gets thin and strange. Sanity damage is real; so is whatever you see.

phantoms.arrive: There is someone standing where you are standing, half a step out of true, mouthing along to the thoughts as you think them.
barks: The one standing inside you thinks your next thought a half-second early. You hear it in your own voice.
It shifts its weight when you shift yours, but always a little wrong, a little late.
phantoms.depart: You breathe out and it breathes out with you, and then only you are breathing.
phantoms.look: It is you, rendered by something that has only ever read about you. The proportions are right. Nothing else is.
phantoms.name: someone standing exactly where you are
phantoms.talk: It answers in your voice, from somewhere inside your chest: "There's no one here but us, and there's no us."

phantoms.arrive: A vertical seam opens in the wall where no seam was, wide enough for one eye, and the eye is open.
barks: The seam widens by a hair. Behind it, the eye tracks you across the room.
Through the gap you can see the room you're in, from the other side, with you standing in it.
phantoms.depart: The seam presses shut and the wall forgets it was ever anything but wall.
phantoms.look: The edges of it are too clean, like a cut in a photograph. What's behind isn't dark. It's more room, wrong-way-round.
phantoms.name: a seam in the wall that is watching
phantoms.talk: The eye does not blink. The seam widens, very slightly, as if leaning closer to listen.

phantoms.arrive: A small figure resolves out of the glare on a nearby surface — a child's shape, edged in cold light, facing the wrong way.
barks: The glare-child raises one arm and points at something behind you. You do not turn around.
It hums a tune you almost recognise, in a key that doesn't exist.
phantoms.depart: The light shifts by an inch and takes the shape of the child with it.
phantoms.look: Look straight at it and it's only a smear of reflected light. Look away and it's a child again, and closer.
phantoms.name: a child made of window-glare

effects.onset_message: Something in the room thins out, and you can see how little is holding it together.

overdose.message: Reality doesn't tear so much as admit it was never solid. Something looks back through the gap, knows your name, and takes a piece of you with it when it goes.

phases.comedown_message: The walls firm up, mostly. The corners are still not quite where you left them.
phases.comeup_message: The light in the room goes thin and grey, as if the world were a print left too long in the sun.
phases.end_message: The room settles back into being only a room. You are fairly sure you are alone. Fairly.

withdrawal.message: The world is too solid, too loud, too certain of itself. You keep checking the corners of the walls for a seam.

name: Glasshollow
